disease_label_per_paper: Cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spinal epidural abscess with paraspinal and psoas abscesses
presentation_summary: 57-year-old woman was admitted with one week of worsening nontraumatic thoracic back pain, 10/10 intensity, worse with motion and relieved by rest.
Physical examination found paraspinal and midline spinal tenderness but no gross or focal neurologic signs; no skin tracks or other signs of active intravenous drug use were detected.
ED vitals showed oral temperature 98.3 F, blood pressure 147/100 mmHg, pulse 96/min, respirations 20/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Labs showed WBC 26.1 x10^9/L with 78% neutrophils, lactate 2.4 mmol/L, sodium 118 mEq/L, chloride 78 mEq/L, CRP >320 mg/L, ESR 75 mm/h, and creatinine 1.9 mg/dL.

MRI showed a large posterior SEA from the lower cervical spine into the upper lumbar spine with moderate canal narrowing and mild cord compression, plus paraspinal cellulitis/myositis, cervical and lumbar paraspinal abscesses, left psoas myositis, and a 2 cm left psoas abscess.
